A flattened rope ring wrapped around the straw hat brim, holding § flowers and § leaves — the cheapest piece in town, and it shows the moment you buy it.
A loop knot at the neck with two tails falling from the collarbone to the chest — it swings with the body as you walk and still hangs when you stand still.
A boxy pack on the back: flap, two bedrolls, two shoulder straps. The first piece you can recognise as gear even from behind.
A coil of hemp rope with a brass buckle and a loose end on the right — an ellipse fitted to the egg-shaped body, so it never sticks out like an iron ring.
Three capes narrowing layer by layer hang down the back with a pair of clasps at the shoulders — a silhouette that tapers downward, the only read you get from behind.
A wooden mask with two sunken eyes, a pointed beak and a pair of ear tufts — it covers the whole face and leaves only two bright silver dots. One of the priciest tiers.
Two round frames, a bridge and two temples, each frame edge carrying a small moth wing — the rings sit in front of the existing eyes, so the pupils never smear.
Two layered plates, one per shoulder, each with a short spike and two brass studs — hung off the shoulder joint so it lifts with the arm when you swing.
